statement: Serial frames use 8N1: one start bit (0), eight data bits LSB first, no parity, one stop bit (1).
Each bit period lasts PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT i_clk cycles.
The serial line is held high when idle.
PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is fixed at elaboration and must be within the legal range 4 to 65535.

not_verified.note: Parameter range fixed at elaboration; not a simulation property.

statement: No idle bit is inserted between the stop bit and the next start bit.
A one-byte holding register keeps each received byte until it is taken.
The receiver detects a start bit on a falling edge and rechecks the start bit in the middle of the bit, rejecting glitches.
The receiver samples each data bit and the stop bit in the middle of the bit.
o_rx_frame_err is set and delivered together with the received byte.
o_rx_overrun pulses.
The transmitter and receiver operate simultaneously and independently of each other (full duplex).
PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT defines the bit period N in i_clk cycles for both transmitter and receiver, default 16, legal range 4 to 65535.
LPARA_UART_HALF_BIT shall equal floor(PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT / 2), the middle-of-bit sampling offset H, using integer division.
The block shall behave as specified for every PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT value from 4 to 65535, both odd and even.

not_verified.note: A sweep over all values 4..65535 is not one simulation. The checks are parameterised and run at N=16, 4 (CHK-014), 5 (CHK-015) and 1024 (CHK-016). The full range is covered by elaboration and synthesis.

statement: The block should stop elaboration with an error message when PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is outside 4 to 65535.

not_verified.note: Elaboration error for an illegal parameter; not a simulation test (D-011: not verified).

statement: i_rst_n is an active-low reset that asserts asynchronously and releases synchronously to i_clk.
When o_tx_ready is 1, the transmitter must accept the byte on i_tx_data at the next i_clk edge.
o_tx_ready must reset to 1.
Bit 0 of i_tx_data must be sent first on o_txd.
o_rx_valid must reset to 0.
o_rx_valid must be 1 when the holding register holds a byte.
The held byte is taken by the consumer at the edge where i_rx_ready is 1.
o_rx_data must reset to 0.
o_rx_data must present the received byte with bit 0 received first, qualified by o_rx_valid.
o_rx_frame_err must reset to 0.
o_rx_frame_err must be 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0, qualified by o_rx_valid.
o_rx_overrun must reset to 0.
o_rx_overrun must pulse for one cycle when a received byte is dropped because the holding register is full.
o_txd must reset to 1 and be high when idle.
i_rxd, asynchronous to i_clk and idle high, must be synchronised inside the block.
All state elements shall be clocked only by the rising edge of i_clk, with no other clock, no gated clock and no latch.

not_verified.note: Single clock, no gated clocks and no latches: checked by lint and synthesis.

statement: Every flip-flop shall take its reset value at once, without waiting for an i_clk edge.
Outputs shall be o_txd = 1, o_tx_ready = 1, o_rx_valid = 0, o_rx_data = 0, o_rx_frame_err = 0, o_rx_overrun = 0.
No transmit byte shall be accepted.
The receiver shall not detect a start bit and shall not deliver a byte.
Both i_rxd synchronizer flip-flops and any flip-flop holding the previous synchronised line value shall reset to 1.
The frame shall be abandoned and o_txd shall become 1 at once.
The partly received frame shall be discarded and shall not produce o_rx_valid, o_rx_frame_err or o_rx_overrun after the release.
The held byte shall be discarded.
The transmitter shall be idle with o_tx_ready = 1 and shall accept a byte at the first edge after the release.
The receiver shall be idle.
The previous synchronised value s(R1-1) shall be taken as 1, so s(R1) = 0 is detected as T0.
Frames shall be sent and received in 8N1 format: start bit 0, eight data bits LSB first, stop bit 1, no parity bit.
The transmitter and receiver shall operate simultaneously and independently.
Activity of the transmitter shall not change the timing or outputs of the receiver, and vice versa.
Every output port shall be driven directly by a flip-flop clocked by i_clk, with no combinational path from any input to any output.
The transmitter shall accept a byte at an edge only when i_tx_valid = 1, o_tx_ready = 1 and i_rst_n = 1.
The transmitter shall capture i_tx_data at the accepting edge E0; i_tx_data at any other edge shall have no effect.
o_tx_ready shall be 1 while the transmitter is idle.
o_tx_ready shall be 0 in the cycles after edges E0 to E0+10N-2 inclusive.
o_tx_ready shall become 1 at edge E0+10N-1, the last cycle of the stop bit.
The transmitter shall not accept a byte and its state shall not depend on i_tx_data.
The transmitter shall not require i_tx_valid to stay 1 until a handshake; if it returns to 0 before a handshake, nothing is sent.
The transmitter shall hold at most one byte, the one being sent, with no additional transmit buffer.
o_txd in the cycle after edge E0+k shall equal frame bit floor(k/N) of D (bit0=0, bit j=D[j-1], bit9=1) for k from 0 to 10N-1.
The start bit of the new frame shall begin at edge E0+10N with no idle cycle after the previous stop bit.
o_txd shall be 1 from edge E0+10N until the edge after which the next accepted frame starts.
o_txd shall be 1 while the transmitter is idle.
i_rxd shall pass through a synchronizer of exactly two flip-flops clocked by i_clk, with no logic between them, before other logic uses it.
The receiver shall be either idle or receiving, and shall be idle after reset, after a glitch and after the stop-bit sample of a frame.
The receiver shall detect a start bit at edge T0 if and only if s(T0-1)=1 and s(T0)=0.
The receiver shall not need the line high longer than the single sample s(T0-1)=1 before a start bit.
At T0+H the receiver shall check the start bit; if s(T0+H)=1 it shall treat it as a glitch, return to idle and receive no byte.
A glitch shall not change o_rx_valid, o_rx_data or o_rx_frame_err, and shall not make o_rx_overrun pulse.
The receiver shall detect a new start bit at any edge T0' > T0+H at which the start condition holds.
The receiver shall go on to receive the frame.
Data bit i (0 to 7) shall be sampled at edge T0+H+(i+1)N, and received byte bit i shall equal s(T0+H+(i+1)N).
The receiver shall sample the stop bit at edge M = T0+H+9N.
Only s(T0-1), s(T0), s(T0+H), the eight data samples and s(M) shall affect a frame result; i_rxd at other edges between T0 and M shall be ignored.
The receiver shall be idle after sampling at M and shall detect a new start bit at any T0' > M where the start condition holds, including M+1.
Every confirmed frame shall complete at M regardless of the value of s(M).
The receiver shall keep sampling and receiving frames; a low i_rx_ready shall not stall or delay it.
The block shall load the frame: o_rx_valid becomes 1, o_rx_data the received byte, o_rx_frame_err the inverse of s(M).
The held byte shall be taken and the new frame loaded at the same edge; o_rx_valid stays 1 and no overrun is reported.
o_rx_valid shall become 0 at that edge.
o_rx_valid, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err shall keep their values.
o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err shall change only when a new byte is loaded or on reset, keeping the last loaded values (0 after reset) while o_rx_valid=0.
i_rx_ready shall have no effect while o_rx_valid=0.
Bytes shall be delivered in the order in which their frames completed.
o_rx_frame_err shall be 1 with a loaded byte if and only if s(M) of that frame was 0.
The byte shall be delivered, held and taken like any other byte, and o_rx_data shall hold its sampled data bits.
The receiver shall not detect a new start bit until s is 1 at one edge and 0 at the next, so a line held at 0 produces exactly one frame.
The block shall drop the new byte and its frame-error flag.
o_rx_overrun shall become 1 at edge V and return to 0 at V+1, being 1 for exactly one cycle.
o_rx_valid, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err shall keep the held byte unchanged.
o_rx_overrun shall be 0 in every cycle except the cycle after an edge at which a byte is dropped.
o_rx_overrun shall not be qualified by o_rx_valid and shall not need a handshake.
o_rx_overrun shall not pulse.
The start bit must appear on o_txd in the first cycle after the accepting handshake edge E0.
The transmit frame must last 10N cycles, with the stop bit ending at edge E0+10N.
o_tx_ready must be 0 for 10N-1 cycles after E0 and become 1 in the last cycle of the stop bit.
The block must never drop an offered byte while o_tx_ready = 0; the upstream block waits.
The transmitter must accept one byte every 10N cycles and produce a continuous stream of frames with no idle cycle between them.
Bytes must be sent on o_txd in the order in which they were accepted.
Delivery must occur at V = T0 + H + 9N + 2 edges, which is 2 edges after the stop-bit sample M.
The receiver must accept frames back to back with no idle bit between them.
After V, o_rx_overrun must be 1 for one cycle and the held byte must remain unchanged.
When the stop-bit sample s(M) is 0, the byte is delivered with o_rx_frame_err = 1.
The new byte is dropped, o_rx_overrun pulses for one cycle and the held byte stays.
No overrun occurs if the held byte is taken at V itself.
The frame-error flag of a dropped byte is not reported.
On a start-bit glitch, no byte, no flag and no pulse is produced.
A low pulse on i_rxd sampled at fewer than H+1 consecutive edges starting at T0 is always rejected.
The receiver delivers byte 0x00 with o_rx_frame_err = 1, or drops it with an overrun pulse under Section 7.8 rules.
The receiver receives no further frame until the line has been sampled as 1 and then as 0.
The receiver stays idle and delivers nothing.
The receiver detects R1 as T0 and processes the frame under Sections 7.4 to 7.8; a line staying low yields one byte 0x00 with o_rx_frame_err = 1.
The transmitter shall not accept the byte and shall not record it.
The block shall do nothing.
Transmit handshake and receive delivery or take in the same cycle shall be handled independently.
Bit-period and sample-offset counting shall not overflow or wrap early at N = 65535.

not_verified.note: N=65535 is not simulated (D-012, 655350 cycles per frame). Counter width and wrap are covered by elaboration and synthesis. Wide-N counting is exercised at N=1024 by CHK-016.

statement: Values of N outside 4 to 65535 are illegal and must not be used.

not_verified.note: Illegal parameter values are excluded at elaboration; no simulation configuration uses them.

statement: CFG-MIN with PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=4 is the smallest legal bit period and must be verified for minimum sampling margins.
The environment shall release i_rst_n synchronously to i_clk, meeting recovery and removal times.

not_verified.note: Environment rule (ENV-001). Applied as a stimulus constraint in all tests: i_rst_n is released synchronously to i_clk.

statement: The environment shall hold i_rst_n at 0 for at least 2 cycles of i_clk at the start of simulation.

not_verified.note: Environment rule (ENV-002). Applied as a stimulus constraint: every simulation starts with i_rst_n=0 for at least 2 i_clk cycles.

statement: The environment shall drive i_tx_valid, i_tx_data and i_rx_ready synchronously to i_clk with no X or Z values.

not_verified.note: Environment rule (ENV-003). Applied as a stimulus constraint: i_tx_valid, i_tx_data and i_rx_ready are driven just after rising edges with no X or Z.

statement: The testbench shall change i_rxd away from rising edges of i_clk, e.g. on the falling edge or at a non-coincident random offset.

not_verified.note: Environment rule (ENV-004). Applied as a stimulus constraint: i_rxd changes only at falling edges of i_clk, including the loopback (designer decision).

statement: i_rxd shall not be X or Z after reset release.

not_verified.note: Environment rule (ENV-004). Applied as a stimulus constraint: i_rxd is never X or Z after reset release.

statement: The synchronizer structure (exactly two flip-flops, no logic between them, REQ-RX-001) shall be checked by lint or structural review.

not_verified.note: Per the designer decision, the synchronizer structure is checked on the RTL at gate D2 (RR-33, nnc rtl-check). Its port-visible latency is checked by CHK-003 and CHK-022.

statement: The reference model shall compute s(E) from i_rxd and apply Sections 7.4 to 7.8 exactly.
The checker shall check REQ-TX-004, REQ-TX-005 and REQ-TX-010 cycle by cycle.
Sampling-point test: drive i_rxd so each bit is correct only at its sampling edge T0+H+(i+1)N and M, wrong at edges just before and after.
Glitch test: low pulses on i_rxd of 1 to H samples are rejected and H+1 samples are accepted as a start bit.
Loopback test: connect o_txd to i_rxd and check the Section 8.5 latency and byte integrity.
Reset tests: assert i_rst_n asynchronously between clock edges in mid-transmit frame, mid-receive frame and while o_rx_valid = 1.
Test line low at reset release (REQ-ERR-003) and break (REQ-ERR-001).
Cover data bytes 0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA and random bytes in both directions.
Cover back-to-back transmit with i_tx_valid held at 1, and transmit with idle gaps of various lengths.
Cover back-to-back receive frames with the next start bit right after the stop bit.
Cover frame error with o_rx_valid = 0, and frame error with the byte dropped by overrun.
Cover overrun, and the case where the held byte is taken at delivery edge V itself (no overrun).
Cover i_rx_ready held at 1, toggling at random, and held at 0 for several frames.
Cover i_tx_valid dropping before a handshake.
Cover transmit and receive active at the same time.
The block shall meet timing at 50 MHz (20 ns period) on GF180MCU for every legal value of PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT.

not_verified.note: Timing closure at 50 MHz on GF180MCU: synthesis/STA.

statement: The RTL shall follow docs/RTL_RULES.md.

not_verified.note: RTL coding rules compliance: rtl-check/lint.

statement: The RTL shall be synthesizable, contain no latches and pass Verilator lint with no warnings.

not_verified.note: Synthesizability, no latches, clean Verilator lint.

statement: All flip-flops shall use the asynchronous active-low reset i_rst_n.

not_verified.note: Every flip-flop using the async reset is structural. Its port-visible effect is covered by CHK-002 and CHK-019.

statement: The two i_rxd synchronizer flip-flops should be marked so synthesis does not merge, duplicate or retime them.

not_verified.note: Synthesis attributes on the synchronizer flops.

statement: The bit-period counters should be only as wide as PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT needs, at most 16 bits.

not_verified.note: Counter width advice; nothing to observe at the ports.

statement: The block should use only the storage the specification requires: transmit shift register, receive shift register, holding register, counters and flags.

not_verified.note: Storage-minimisation advice. The port-visible 'no extra transmit buffer' behaviour is checked by CHK-032.

statement: o_tx_ready must be 1 (its idle value) while i_rst_n = 0, since no handshake is possible during reset.
The receiver samples the middle of each bit H = floor(N/2) edges after T0, then every N edges.
o_rx_valid is delivered at V = M + 2, where M is the sample edge of i_rxd and 2 is the synchronizer latency.
The new byte is loaded and no overrun occurs.
A new start requires a 1-to-0 transition on i_rxd, so a break yields only one byte.
The synchronizer resets to 1; a low i_rxd at reset release is detected as a start bit.
o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err keep the last loaded values, and are 0 after reset.
The frame is abandoned, o_txd goes to 1 at once and the byte is lost.
The frame-error flag of a dropped byte is not reported.
An elaboration error should be raised for illegal parameter values; this is not verified.

not_verified.note: Elaboration error for illegal parameters is recommended but not verified (D-011).

statement: CFG-ODD (5) and CFG-WIDE (1024) are simulated; CFG-MAX (65535) is not simulated and is covered by elaboration and synthesis only.
No area budget is required for GF180MCU; area is reported, not checked.

not_verified.note: Area is reported from synthesis, not checked.

statement: The 50 MHz target applies at the slow corner (GF180MCU SS, 125 C, 4.5 V).

not_verified.note: PVT corner for STA (SS, 125 C, 4.5 V).
